correctness.rationale: Reassessed the complete repaired claim. Strict positivity and monotone decrease follow from η_n=x_n+βy_n²>0; (exp(η_n)-1)/x_n≥1 gives a trait-independent O(1/n) bound. For 0<s<2, q=1-s contracts; y_n tends to zero and x_{n+1}/x_n tends to one. For each fixed lag, its ratio to x_n tends to one, and the weighted sum is justified by a geometric bound |q| exp(ε)<1 for late x-values and relative exponential decay for the finitely many early terms. The same argument with x_n² and 2ε applies to d_{n+1}=q d_n+x_n-x_{n+1}. It gives y_n/x_n→1 and then d_n/x_n²→1/s. First w_{n+1}-w_n=1+O(x_n) gives w_n=n+O(log n); the next increment is 1+(β+1/2)x_n+O(x_n²), whose difference from 1+(β+1/2)/(n+1) is summable. At s=2 the exact telescoping signed trait identity gives a uniformly convergent alternating tail with remainder at most x_N, so A is continuous in the initial trait. Strict alternating-tail inequalities give opposite signs at traits 0 and 2x_0, proving at least one zero, not uniqueness. For A≠0 one has y_n=(-1)^n A+O(x_n) and limiting geometric ratio exp(-βA²) below one. Consequently x_n and η_n-βA² are absolutely summable, verifying the positive finite exponential prefactor and absolute convergence of the amplitude series. For A=0 the strict tail bound gives 0<y_n<2x_n. The two-step normalized trait identity is correctly inverted by multiplying by x_{n+2} and telescoping with vanishing terminal term. Initially b_n=O(x_n²), yielding p_n=O(1/n); after this bootstrap, η_{n+1}-η_n=-x_n²+O(x_n³) and the quadratic exponential terms contribute another -x_n², so b_n=-2x_n²+O(x_n³). The step-two cubic tail is asymptotic to 1/(4n²), giving np_n→1/2, and the reciprocal clock follows as before. Since x_n∼1/n in that branch, the amplitude series is conditional exactly there, as now stated.
